No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

In this discussion you ask whose labour and lives survive in archaeological evidence.

It is run as a guided conversation, online or on your campus, and works best with a group that is ready to argue a point.

What it covers

  • Domestic assemblage case study
  • Bioarchaeological interpretation caveats
  • Small-group bias audit
  • Research question clinic

How the time is spent

  1. Domestic assemblage case study 15 min

  2. Bioarchaeological interpretation caveats 25 min

  3. Small-group bias audit 30 min

  4. Research question clinic 20 min

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Ask whose labour and lives survive in the evidence of a domestic assemblage.
  • Explain the caveats involved in interpreting bioarchaeological evidence.
  • Audit an interpretation for bias and frame a research question of your own.

You take away

An interpretation sheet with questions to ask on site and suggested reading.
